references.name: Fischer Black & Myron Scholes
references.desc: "The Pricing of Options and Corporate Liabilities" (1973)
references.connection:
Black-Scholes formula is the mathematical
foundation for all option pricing, delta calculation,
and probability analysis throughout the book.

references.name: Robert Merton
Fischer Black
references.desc: Black model for futures options pricing
references.connection:
The Black model (Black-Scholes with r=0, discounted)
is the standard for pricing futures options in
Chapters 34–35.

references.name: Chicago Board Options Exchange
references.desc: Founded 1973; creator of standardized listed equity options
references.connection:
CBOE's creation made every strategy in the book
possible by standardizing strikes, expirations,
and clearing through the OCC.

references.name: Options Clearing Corporation
references.desc: Guarantor and issuer of all listed options
references.connection:
OCC's guarantee eliminates counterparty risk,
enabling the liquid secondary market that makes
rolling, spreading, and follow-up practical.

references.name: CME Group
references.connection:
SPAN's 16-scenario array determines futures options
margin requirements and enables portfolio-level
netting of offsetting positions.

references.name: RAMBUS Inc.
references.desc: Technology company; case study in volatility regimes
references.connection:
McMillan uses RMBS to illustrate how volatility
regimes can shift permanently, rendering historical
comparison ranges obsolete and trapping vol sellers.
